results.title: [2410.08554] Integrated adaptive coherent LiDAR for 4D bionic vision
results.content: # Title:Integrated adaptive coherent LiDAR for 4D bionic vision. View a PDF of the paper titled Integrated adaptive coherent LiDAR for 4D bionic vision, by Ruixuan Chen and 19 other authors. A bionic LiDAR that can mimic human-like vision by adaptively gazing at selected regions of interest within a broad field of view is crucial to achieve high-resolution imaging in an energy-saving and cost-effective manner. Using the dynamic zoom-in capability and the coherent FMCW scheme, we achieve a state-of-the-art resolution of 0.012 degrees, providing up to 15 times the resolution of conventional 3D LiDAR sensors, with 115 equivalent scanning lines and 4D parallel imaging. | Cite as: | arXiv:2410.08554 [physics.optics] |. |  | (or  arXiv:2410.08554v1 [physics.optics] for this version) |. results.title: Top 10 Emerging Trends In Computer Science Engineering | BNMIT
results.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are pivotal forces driving innovation across industries. AI and ML offer automated solutions, personalized experiences, and data-driven decision-making. Edge computing enables data processing closer to the source, enhancing real-time analytics. This technology has found its footing in the Internet of Things (IoT) and offers swift data processing, enabling IoT devices to respond instantly. Emerging technologies, such as AI-driven threat detection and blockchain encryption, are being employed to fortify data security. Quantum computing promises to transform the landscape of problem-solving in fields such as drug discovery, materials science, and optimization, making it one of the most intriguing and promising trends in Computer Science Engineering for 2023. As AR and VR advance, they will revolutionize human-computer interaction, offer innovative solutions to multifaceted challenges, and solidify their status as pivotal trends in Computer Science Engineering for 2023. As we venture into 2023, the influence of IoT is undeniable, making it a pivotal trend in Computer Science Engineering. 5G’s implications reverberate across industries, making it a foundational trend in Computer Science Engineering. Data Science and Big Data Analytics are indispensable tools for data-driven decision-making. The impact of data science and big data analytics in transforming industries and enhancing decision-making processes solidifies their standing as core trends in Computer Science Engineering. The proliferation of these applications solidifies NLP and Conversational AI as pivotal trends in Computer Science Engineering for 2023. ## **Applications of Emerging Trends In Computer Science Engineering**. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are used to detect fraud in financial transactions, offer personalised suggestions in retail, and support medical diagnostics for better healthcare results. Big data analytics and data science may help with corporate intelligence, tailor marketing campaigns, and guide healthcare decision-making. In this blog, we’ve explored the top 10 emerging trends in Computer Science Engineering for 2023. From the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning to the game-changing impact of Edge Computing, the rise of blockchain technology, and the promise of Quantum Computing, these trends shape the future of our digital world. Data Science and Big Data Analytics enable data-driven decision-making, and Natural Language Processing and Conversational AI systems are redefining communication.

results.title: Areas of Research | Computer Science and Engineering at Michigan
results.content: Home > Research > Areas of Research. # Areas of Research in CSE. The Computer Science and Engineering Division (CSE) at Michigan Engineering advances research across a broad range of disciplines, from artificial intelligence to secure systems and theory. Explore our key areas of expertise and the innovative work shaping the future of computing. ## Artificial Intelligence. Advancing the theory and application of intelligent systems, including machine learning and perception, natural language processing, robotics, and trustworthy AI. ## Chip Design, Architecture, & Emerging Devices. Designing efficient, secure, and future-ready hardware architectures and novel devices to power next-generation computing. ## Databases & Data Mining. Building innovative systems and infrastructure for big data, including real-time processing, integration, analytics, and human-data interaction. ## Embedded & Mobile Systems. Designing reliable systems for vehicles, sensors, wearables, and smart devices in cyber-physical and IoT environments. ## Formal Methods & Automated Reasoning. Developing rigorous, automated approaches to verify software and hardware correctness, ensuring reliability and safety in complex systems. ## Human-Computer Interaction. Creating technology that enhances how people interact, learn, and collaborate while exploring accessibility, mobile interfaces, educational tools, and social computing. ## Languages, Compilers, & Runtime Systems. Advancing programming languages, compiler technologies, and runtime systems to maximize software performance, efficiency, adaptability, and security across platforms. ## Networking, Operating Systems, & Distributed Systems. Building reliable, secure, and high-performance infrastructure to underpin network, wireless, and cloud environments while providing seamless connectivity, scalable services, and robust operating systems. ## Secure, Trustworthy, & Reliable Systems. Protecting digital systems through secure hardware and software, enhanced system reliability, and strengthened privacy. ## Theory of Computation. Exploring foundational principles underpinning computer science across cryptography, graph theory, quantum computing, combinatorics, and optimization. ## Warehouse-Scale & Parallel Systems. Designing scalable and efficient hardware and software architectures for cloud, data centers, and high-performance computing powering modern science and enterprise.
